signum, signī n.

noun, second declension

a military standard

The standard of a division of the army. Soldiers follow it, signa sequī (Sall. J. 80.2), march off with it, signa ferre (Caes. BG 1.39), and leave the ranks, ab signīs discēdere (Caes. BG 5.16; all from Lewis & Short). The bearer is the signifer.

Other words

  • aquila, aquilae f. — the eagle, the standard of a legion

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.24: aquila argentea (Lewis & Short); Andresian p. 48

    The legion’s standard, as against the signa of its cohorts (Lewis & Short).

  • vexillum, vexillī n. — a cloth banner

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 2.20 (Lewis & Short); Andresian p. 48

    See flag.

See also flag, soldier, eagle.
